description: Masjid-e-Tooba, also known as Gol Masjid ('Round Mosque'), is a mosque in Karachi, Pakistan, per Wikipedia: construction began in 1966 and was completed in 1969, designed by Pakistani architect Babar Hameed Chauhan with structural engineer Zaheer Haider Naqvi. The prayer hall sits under a wider dome without any pillar or column - the dome is 212 feet (65 m) in diameter, the mosque holds up to 5,000 people, has a single minaret 120 feet (37 m) high, and Wikipedia describes it as the largest single-dome mosque in the world with no pillars. description: Rescue 1122 is an emergency service that serves almost all regions of Pakistan including Sindh and is accessible by dialling 1122 from any phone within Pakistan, per Wikipedia; it was launched in 2004 in Lahore as a professional pre-hospital emergency service and later expanded to include fire and rescue response under a united command structure. In Karachi the OSM evidence consists of individual rescue stations (e.g. the SIEHS-1122 North Nazimabad station pinned here); it is a public emergency service, not a visitor venue.

notes: PIN CAVEAT: there is no OSM element for 'Rescue 1122 Sindh/Karachi headquarters' (Overpass searches for 'Rescue 1122', '1122', amenity=fire_station and emergency=ambulance_station across the Karachi bbox returned exactly one Karachi 1122 element); node 12227788485 is a single named station ('SIEHS-1122 North Nazimabad Station (7)') and the coordinates describe that station, not the service area. The official site rescue1122.org is a JavaScript app; its served HTML carries the 1122 emergency number in title/meta text ('Rescue1122 Emergency Services'), which is the only contact value published - no email and no Karachi line printed, so email is null and confidence stays partially-verified (a hotline, not a venue contact/timetable). The catalogue's 'Stations across all seven districts' was not verifiable from official pages. Commons photo explicitly names 'RESCUE 1122' but shows the Okara (Punjab) station, not a Karachi one - kept because the record subject is the Rescue 1122 service itself, with this caveat published rather than implying a Karachi scene.

name: University of Karachi
address: University Road, Karachi-75270 (official uok.edu.pk); OSM: University of Karachi (campus way), University Road, Gulshan-e-Iqbal Town, Karachi

contact.email: registrar@uok.edu.pk (printed in the official uok.edu.pk homepage contact block)

description: The University of Karachi is a public research university established in June 1951 by an act of Parliament as a successor to the University of Sindh, per Wikipedia; with a student body of tens of thousands on a campus spanning over 490 hectares (1,200 acres), it is described there as one of the largest universities in Pakistan, with over 53 departments and 19 research institutes under nine faculties. Its official site states 'University of Karachi - Official Website | Est. 1951' with the University Road, Karachi-75270 address and a registrar email.

notes: Pin is the large OSM campus way (amenity=university, name:en 'University of Karachi'), centre 24.9437, 67.1206, matching Wikipedia's coordinate (~24.94, 67.12). The official homepage footer/contact block prints 'Address: University Road, Karachi-75270' and 'Email: registrar@uok.edu.pk' - a registrar office email rather than a public visitor contact, and no phone number or visiting hours appear in the fetchable HTML (the site is partly JS-rendered), so phone is null and the record is marked verified only on the strength of the printed venue email; if the generator treats registrar email as insufficient, this is a candidate for downgrade to partially-verified. Catalogue address 'Stadium Road, Gulshan-e-Iqbal' conflicts with the official 'University Road' and was replaced. Commons photo names the campus's Silver Jubilee Gate explicitly (November 2022).
